chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from some of them, from Abu al-Mi'za, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him: 'A slave man had a free woman under his ownership (as a concubine), and he accused her of adultery.' He said: 'What do the people of Kufa say regarding her?' I said: 'She is lashed.' He said: 'No, but he performs li'an with her just as a free man performs li'an.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of li'an when a slave man accuses his free female concubine of adultery?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration to clarify the specific application of *li'an* (mutual imprecation) in cases involving a slave man and a free female concubine (*Umm Walad*). The Imam rejects the prevailing opinion of the people of Kufa, who held that the slave would be lashed, establishing instead that the slave performs *li'an* just as a free man would, thereby exempting him from the *hadd* of flogging. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of concubines in Shia jurisprudence, where the primary mechanism for resolving their adultery accusations is imprecation rather than corporal punishment.
